subproblem.title: Weight measures of two represented currents agree on an open set where the currents agree (supplied step 5)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let S, T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) be currents represented by integer multiplicity triples RS and RT in ℝ^P (RS.Represents S, RT.Represents T), and let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Suppose S(ω) = T(ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Then the weight measures agree on O: RS.measure⌞O = RT.measure⌞O (Measure.restrict).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RS RT : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (O : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → RS.Represents S → RT.Represents T → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ O → S ω = T ω) → RS.measure.restrict O = RT.measure.restrict O
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the selected node's supplied proof ('S = T on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K', so μ_S = μ_T there'). The supplied proof obtains this from part (c) of im_mass_measure applied in ℝ^P ∖ K' to restricted representations. The argument below uses only the mass formula of the sibling mass_support (Submission.dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support) and the uniqueness of measures on a π-system, which avoids building representations on the smaller domain.
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]; for an IMRep R, R.measure = (μ⌞R.carrier).withDensity R.mult. For a current Z in ℝ^P and a set W, Z.massOn W = sup{ofReal(Z(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m W}, where ω is admissible iff ω is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x (Simon 6.2.5).
1. Equal masses inside O. Let W ⊆ O. Every admissible ω for W has tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ O, so S(ω) = T(ω) by hypothesis. The two sets {ofReal(S ω)} and {ofReal(T ω)}, indexed by the same admissible forms, therefore coincide (Set.image_congr), and S.massOn W = T.massOn W.
2. Equal measures of open subsets of O. Let W be open with W ⊆ O. By mass_support (with U = ℝ^P open) applied to (S, RS) and to (T, RT): RS.measure(W) = S.massOn W = T.massOn W = RT.measure(W).
3. Local finiteness. For every IMRep R in ℝ^P and every real r: R.measure(B̄(0, r)) = ∫⁻_{R.carrier ∩ B̄(0, r)} θ dμ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict), which is finite by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set B̄(0, r) ⊆ ℝ^P.
4. Uniqueness. Put μ₁ := RS.measure⌞O and μ₂ := RT.measure⌞O. The open subsets of ℝ^P form a π-system (isPiSystem_isOpen) that generates the Borel σ-algebra, which is the σ-algebra of ℝ^P (BorelSpace.measurable_eq). For every open G, G ∩ O is open and contained in O, so by step 2 μ₁(G) = RS.measure(G ∩ O) = RT.measure(G ∩ O) = μ₂(G) (Measure.restrict_apply, G measurable). The open balls B_i := B(0, i + 1), i ∈ ℕ, belong to the π-system, cover ℝ^P (iUnion_ball_nat_succ), and μ₁(B_i) ≤ RS.measure(B̄(0, i + 1)) < ∞ by step 3. Two measures that agree on a generating π-system containing a countable cover by sets of finite measure are equal (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). Hence μ₁ = μ₂. ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the mass_support statement as a hypothesis; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: Forms admissible for M_W with W ⊆ O give equal values on S and T, so M_W(S) = M_W(T).
By mass_support, RS.measure(W) = RT.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ O.
Both measures are finite on closed balls (locallyIntegrable_mult).
μ⌞O is determined by its values on the π-system of open sets (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion with the balls B(0, i + 1)).

audit.reason: Agreement on supported test forms gives equal local masses and hence equal weights on open subsets of O. Compact-set finiteness supplies the finite ball cover needed for generating-π-system uniqueness. The sole declared dependency suffices.

subproblem.title: Projection invariance: an integer multiplicity triple carried by a subspace V is fixed by the orthogonal projection onto V (supplied step 1, q_#T = T)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q := V.starProjection, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) whose weight measure μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^m⌞M gives no mass to ℝ^P ∖ V. Then for every m-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (no smoothness, support or integrability assumption) R.action(q^#ω) = R.action(ω), where q^#ω = affinePullbackForm q 0 ω, (q^#ω)(x) = ω(0 + q x)∘Λ^m q, and R.action(η) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^m(x). (This is q_#τ(M, θ, ξ) = τ(M, θ, ξ), supplied step 1.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), R.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m, R.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 ω) = R.action ω
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected node's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2, chapter-07.txt lines 361–364: spt C ⊆ T_xN), which states that H^m-a.e. x ∈ M has its approximate tangent plane in V and hence Λ_m q ξ(x) = ξ(x). The argument below is that step with the details filled in. It uses the sibling flat_tangent (Submission.atsm_approxTangent_le_of_flat) in place of the supplied 'approximate tangent planes of M and of M ∩ V agree, and a tangent plane of a subset of V lies in V'; flat_tangent states the needed conclusion directly for the set M.
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult (ℕ-valued, θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient; q := V.starProjection; V is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional) and Borel.
1. M ∖ V is H^m-null. By definition R.measure = (μ⌞M).withDensity θ, so by withDensity_apply (Vᶜ is measurable), Measure.restrict_restrict and Set.inter_comm, 0 = R.measure(Vᶜ) = ∫⁻_{Vᶜ} θ d(μ⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ Vᶜ} θ dμ. Since θ(x) ≥ 1 for x ∈ M (mult_pos), μ(M ∩ Vᶜ) = ∫⁻_{M∩Vᶜ} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩Vᶜ} θ dμ = 0 (setLIntegral_mono'). Hence μ(M ∖ V) = 0, and consequently μ⌞M-a.e. x lies in V (ae_restrict_iff' with M measurable, together with measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem).
2. Orientation field. By the IMRep field orients, for μ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q: there is an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) with span(τ_1, …, τ_m) = Q such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all m-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
3. Approximate tangent planes lie in V. Fix x satisfying both step 1 (x ∈ V) and step 2 (with Q, τ). Apply flat_tangent with N := V (as a set), the set M, the point x, the plane Q and T := V. Its hypotheses hold: (i) H^m(M ∖ V) = 0 by step 1; (ii) V is flat at x along V: given ε > 0 take ρ := 1; for z ∈ V the vector t := z − x lies in V (x, z ∈ V) and ‖z − x − t‖ = 0 ≤ ε‖z − x‖; (iii) HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q by step 2. Hence Q ≤ V. Thus every τ_i ∈ span(τ) = Q ⊆ V, so q τ_i = τ_i, and q x = x since x ∈ V (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff).
4. Pointwise identity. For x as in step 3 and every m-covector α, (α.compContinuousLinearMap q)(τ_1, …, τ_m) = α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m) = α(τ_1, …, τ_m), so ξ(x)(α∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(α) in both sign cases of step 2. Taking α := ω(0 + q x) = ω(x) gives ξ(x)((q^#ω)(x)) = ξ(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(ω(x)), hence θ(x)·ξ(x)((q^#ω)(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)).
5. Conclusion. By steps 1–4 the integrands of R.action(q^#ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(q^#ω) dμ and R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ·ξ(ω) dμ agree μ⌞M-almost everywhere. Bochner integrals of a.e.-equal functions are equal (integral_congr_ae; this needs no integrability, since both sides are 0 for a non-integrable function), so R.action(q^#ω) = R.action(ω). ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the flat_tangent statement as a hypothesis; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: θ ≥ 1 on M and μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 give H^m(M ∖ V) = 0, so H^m⌞M-a.e. x lies in V.
At such x, flat_tangent with N = T = V (flatness is trivial: t = z − x) puts the approximate tangent plane Q of M, oriented by ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τ_m, inside V.
Then qτ_i = τ_i and q x = x, so ξ(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q) = ξ(x)(ω(x)).
The integrands of R.action(q^#ω) and R.action(ω) agree a.e., so the integrals are equal.

audit.reason: Positive multiplicity converts weight concentration into carrier nullity outside V. The declared flat_tangent dependency puts the oriented planes inside V, so projection fixes the integrands almost everywhere. Integral congruence proves the exact arbitrary-form statement without an integrability assumption.

subproblem.title: Orthogonal projection onto V does not increase mass: M_O(T + q_#X) ≤ μ_{T+X}(q⁻¹(O)) when T is carried by V (supplied step 4)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q := V.starProjection, let T, X, S' ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and let RT, RX be integer multiplicity triples in ℝ^P with RT.Represents T and RX.Represents X. Assume RT.measure(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, and that K ⊆ ℝ^P is compact with RX.measure(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0. Assume S'(ω) = T(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), where q^#ω = affinePullbackForm q 0 ω. Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R in ℝ^P with R.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω) for every test form ω (so R represents every current Z with Z(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω); the contract has no + on currents, and in the parent Z = S = T + (S − T)), and S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)) for every set O ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T X S' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RT RX : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (K : Set (Euclid P)), RT.Represents T → RX.Represents X → RT.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → IsCompact K → RX.measure Kᶜ = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, S' ω = T ω + RX.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))) → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = T ω + X ω) ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure (V.starProjection ⁻¹' O)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the selected node's supplied proof (projection does not increase mass: |Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| ≤ Π|qτ_i| ≤ 1 by Hadamard's inequality, hence M_{W*}(q_#S) ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(W*))), together with q_#T = T from its step 1. Here S' = T + q_#X plays the role of q_#S = q_#T + q_#X, and the representation R of T + X (= S) is built so that its action is additive on the non-compactly supported forms q^#ω.
Siblings used: int_combination (Submission.rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination), projection_invariance (Submission.idtp_fons_cs_sp_action_starProjection_eq), orient_comp (Submission.dtc_bc_lc_pf_unitOrientation_comp) and pairing_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le).
Notation: μ := H^m = μHE[m]. For an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for carrier, mult and orient, and F_R(x) := 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) (R.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R.mult y : ℝ) • R.orient y)). ‖·‖ is the operator norm of a covector or a linear map, |·|_E the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm). q is an orthogonal projection, so ‖q‖ ≤ 1 (starProjection_norm_le); V is closed.
1. Action as a global integral. For every IMRep R and every m-form β, F_R(x)(β(x)) = 1_{M_R}(x)·θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x)), so R.action(β) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R ξ_R(β) dμ = ∫ F_R(x)(β(x)) dμ(x) (integral_indicator, M_R measurable). If x ↦ θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable, then x ↦ F_R(x)(β(x)) is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff).
2. Carriers. If C is measurable and R.measure(Cᶜ) = 0, then μ⌞M_R-a.e. x lies in C. Indeed 0 = R.measure(Cᶜ) = ∫⁻_{M_R ∩ Cᶜ} θ_R dμ (withDensity_apply, restrict_restrict) ≥ μ(M_R ∩ Cᶜ) because θ_R ≥ 1 on M_R; conclude with ae_restrict_iff'.
3. Projected orientation bound. For every IMRep R, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x and every m-covector α: |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E. Proof: by the field orients, for μ⌞M_R-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R x) Q, i.e. ξ_R(x) = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_m for an orthonormal basis τ of Q. The first part of orient_comp with L := q gives |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E·‖q‖^m (in Simon's terms |⟨α, Λ_m q ξ⟩| = |α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m)| ≤ |α|_E·Π_i|qτ_i|, Hadamard's inequality). Since ‖q‖ ≤ 1 and |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), ‖q‖^m ≤ 1 (pow_le_one₀) and |ξ_R(x)(α∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |α|_E.
4. The combined triple. Apply int_combination with U = ℝ^P (open), R₁ = RT, R₂ = RX and p₁ = p₂ = 1. It gives an IMRep R with F_R = F_RT + F_RX μ-a.e.
5. Additivity. Let β be an m-form such that x ↦ θ_RT ξ_RT(β) is μ⌞M_RT-integrable and x ↦ θ_RX ξ_RX(β) is μ⌞M_RX-integrable. By steps 1 and 4, R.action(β) = ∫ F_R(β) dμ = ∫ (F_RT + F_RX)(β) dμ (integral_congr_ae) = ∫ F_RT(β) dμ + ∫ F_RX(β) dμ (integral_add, integrability from step 1) = RT.action(β) + RX.action(β).
6. Test forms; the first conclusion. Let ω be a test form. It is continuous (hence a.e. strongly measurable for every measure) with compact support C := tsupport ω, hence bounded by some B (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and ω(x) = 0 off C (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). So pairing_bound (with U = ℝ^P, F := ω) shows that θ_R ξ_R(ω) is μ⌞M_R-integrable for every IMRep R in ℝ^P. Step 5 gives R.action(ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(ω) = T(ω) + X(ω), since RT represents T and RX represents X.
7. Pull-backs of test forms. Fix a test form ω, let B bound ‖ω‖ and put β := q^#ω, β(x) = ω(0 + q x)∘Λ^m q. Then β is continuous (composition of ω, x ↦ q x and the continuous linear map α ↦ α∘Λ^m q) and ‖β(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω(q x)‖·‖q‖^m ≤ B (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le, ‖q‖ ≤ 1).
 General principle: let R be an IMRep, D a closed set, C a compact set with R.measure(Dᶜ) = 0 and β(x) = 0 for x ∈ D ∖ C. Then θ_R ξ_R(β) is μ⌞M_R-integrable. Indeed F := 1_D·β is a.e. strongly measurable (β is continuous and D is Borel), vanishes off C (on D ∖ C because β does, and off D by definition), and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x (B ≥ ‖β(x)‖ ≥ 0, which also covers x ∉ D where F(x) = 0), so pairing_bound gives integrability of θ_R ξ_R(F). By step 2, F = β μ⌞M_R-a.e., so θ_R ξ_R(β) is integrable (Integrable.congr).
 (a) For RX take D = C = K (compact, hence closed); the vanishing condition is empty.
 (b) For RT take D = V and C = V ∩ tsupport ω (compact). If x ∈ V ∖ tsupport ω, then q x = x and ω(q x) = ω(x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 Hence step 5 applies to β, and with projection_invariance (applicable because RT.measure(Vᶜ) = 0) R.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(q^#ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = RT.action(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = T(ω) + RX.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
8. Mass bound; the second conclusion. Fix O ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ω be admissible for S'.massOn O, i.e. tsupport ω ⊆ O and |ω(y)|_E ≤ 1 for all y, and let β = q^#ω. By step 7, ofReal(S'(ω)) = ofReal(R.action β) ≤ ofReal(|R.action β|) ≤ ∫⁻_{M_R} |θ_R(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x))| dμ (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm). For μ⌞M_R-a.e. x (step 3):
 - if q x ∈ tsupport ω, then |ξ_R(x)(β(x))| = |ξ_R(x)(ω(q x)∘Λ^m q)| ≤ |ω(q x)|_E ≤ 1;
 - if q x ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(q x) = 0, so β(x) = 0.
 So the integrand is at most θ_R(x)·1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)}(x), and ∫⁻_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dμ = R.measure(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) (lintegral_indicator and withDensity_apply; q⁻¹(tsupport ω) is closed, hence measurable) ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)), since tsupport ω ⊆ O. As S'.massOn O is the supremum of ofReal(S'(ω)) over admissible ω (sSup_le), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure(q⁻¹(O)). ∎
Formalization note: this proof was compiled after import GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the statements of the four siblings as hypotheses; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: int_combination gives R with vector density F_R = F_RT + F_RX a.e., so R.action is additive on forms whose pairings with RT and RX are integrable.

Test forms and the pull-backs q^#ω are integrable against RT and RX (pairing_bound; RT lives on V where q^#ω vanishes off tsupport ω, RX lives on the compact K). Hence R represents T + X and, by projection_invariance, R.action(q^#ω) = S'(ω).
For admissible ω with tsupport ω ⊆ O, |S'(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M_R} θ_R 1_{q⁻¹(tsupport ω)} dH^m = μ_R(q⁻¹(tsupport ω)) ≤ μ_R(q⁻¹(O)).

audit.reason: The combined vector density gives the required representation. Integrability of pullbacks is justified separately using V ∩ tsupport ω and compact K, making action additivity legitimate. Projection invariance and the coefficient-norm contraction then prove the bound for every O, without assuming O measurable or S' integer multiplicity.
